chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: It is unpre­ dictable; it carries a massive impact; and, after the fact, we concoct an explanation that makes it appear less random, and more predictable, than it was.

text: The astonishing success of Google was a black swan; so was 9/11.

The astonishing success of Google was a
 black swan; so was 9/11.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: For Nassim Nicholas Taleb, black swans underlie almost everything about our world, from the rise of religions to events in our own personal lives.
text_raw:
For Nassim Nicholas
 Taleb, black swans underlie almost everything
 about our world, from the rise of religions to
 events in our own personal lives.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: Why do we not acknowledge the phenomenon of black swans until after they occur?
text_raw:
Why do we not acknowledge the phenomenon
 of black swans until after they occur?

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: Part of the answer, according to Taleb, is that humans are hardwired to learn specifics when they should be focused on generalities.
text_raw:
Part of the
 answer, according to Taleb, is that humans are
 hardwired to learn specifics when they should
 be focused on generalities.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: We concentrate on things we already know and time and time again fail to take into consideration what we don't know.
text_raw:
We concentrate on
 things we already know and time and time again
 fail to take into consideration what we don't know.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: We are, therefore, unable to truly estimate oppor­ tunities, too vulnerable to the impulse to simplify, narrate, and categorize, and not open enough to rewarding those who can imagine the "impossible." For years, Taleb has studied how we fool our­ selves into thinking we know more than we actually do.
text_raw:
We are, therefore, unable to truly estimate oppor­

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: We restrict our thinking to the irrelevant and inconsequential, while large events continue to surprise us and shape our world.

text: Now, in this reve­ latory book, Taleb explains everything we know about what we don't know.
